name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield near 5.2% ahead of an expected rate rise on 5 Nov
state: The 10-year gilt yield fell to about 5.3% on 2 Nov and was near 5.2% on 3 Nov, below its October high near 5.4%, a multi-year peak (Trading Economics). A Bank of England rise, its first since 2023, is widely expected on 5 Nov. Auctions have been orderly as of 4 Nov.
for_you: High gilt yields keep fixed mortgage rates elevated; borrowers remortgaging soon are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Gilt yields near multi-decade highs = Watch; no BoE intervention

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK gilt yields hold near multi-year highs

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
